chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying to Humran ibn A'yn: 'O Humran! Look at the one who is below you in capability, and do not look at the one who is above you in capability, for that is more contenting for you with what has been apportioned for you, and more likely to earn you increase from your Lord. And know that a small, constant deed done with certainty is more preferable in the presence of Allah, glorified is His remembrance, than a large deed done without certainty. And know that there is no piety more beneficial than avoiding the prohibitions of Allah and refraining from harming the believers and backbiting them, and no life more enjoyable than good character, and no wealth more beneficial than contentment with the sufficient little, and no ignorance more harmful than self-conceit.'
ai.seo_question: What are the key ethical teachings on contentment and character in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) instructs Humran ibn A'yn to cultivate *qana'ah* (contentment) by focusing on those less fortunate, a practice rooted in Shia ethical tradition to secure divine favor and prevent envy. The Imam further elevates the quality of consistency and certainty (*yaqin*) in worship over mere quantity, while identifying the avoidance of *maharim* (divine prohibitions) and harm to believers as the essence of piety (*wara'*). This teaching underscores the Shia emphasis on inner spiritual states and social ethics as the true measures of a believer's worth.

en.hubeali: H 14786 – A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Saalim who said:

I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying to Humraan Bin Ayn: ‘O Humraan! Look to the one who is below you in the capability, and do not look at the one who is above you in the capability, for that would be contentment for you with what Allahazwj has Distributed for you, and you would be more likely to receive more from your Lordazwj. And know that a small amount of deeds with certainty are more preferable in the Presence of Allahazwj than the numerous deeds performed without certainty. And know that there is no devoutness which is more beneficial than avoiding the Prohibitions of Allahazwj and the restraint from hurting the Believers and back-biting against them, and no life more enjoyable than good manners, and no wealth more beneficial than contentment with less, and no ignorance more harmful than ‘الْعُجْبِ’ the self-conceit’.
